hypothesis: FSM baseline itself is unreliable
evidence: fsm_results.csv: 12/20, 7/20, 7/20
counter-evidence: Some fixed scenarios succeed
recommended diagnostic: paired zero-residual checkpoint test

hypothesis: PPO residual is too large and destroys the FSM
evidence: final-policy executed residual is near zero; saturation 0
counter-evidence: Older diagnostics may contain nonzero residual
recommended diagnostic: evaluate an explicitly chosen nonzero checkpoint

hypothesis: PPO residual is too small to change the FSM
evidence: residual_action_statistics.png and identical final outcomes
counter-evidence: Raw policy outputs are nonzero before phase/state projection
recommended diagnostic: log gate occupancy and executed residual during training

hypothesis: Actions are heavily clipped
evidence: episodes residual_saturation_rate=0; telemetry policy clip fraction ~0
counter-evidence: Phase gain has a hard clip but is rarely reached
recommended diagnostic: retain saturation instrumentation

hypothesis: Workspace projection removes wheel-center residual
evidence: runtime has no workspace projection; invalid IK falls back to baseline
counter-evidence: The specialized action projection removes channels before IK
recommended diagnostic: separately log action projection and IK fallback

hypothesis: IK branch or joint clipping breaks continuity
evidence: nearest-reference branch selection; canonical terminal IK invalid counts are zero
counter-evidence: Per-step joint target rate limiting can alter requested motion
recommended diagnostic: log requested-vs-final wheel-center displacement

hypothesis: Wheel-speed residual causes slip or collision
evidence: v34 final executed wheel-speed residual is effectively zero; FSM has same collision pattern
counter-evidence: Earlier v31-v33 diagnostics tested wheel corrections
recommended diagnostic: only test under registered diagnostic label

hypothesis: PPO optimizes progress while ignoring support transfer
evidence: progress weight 8; Method B CoM weight 0; no training component telemetry
counter-evidence: success, collision, phase-progress and top-contact terms exist
recommended diagnostic: log per-term returns by phase

hypothesis: Method B has no CoM reward, so stability improvement is not expected
evidence: ppo_without_com.yaml com_margin_weight=0.0
counter-evidence: pitch/slip/tilt penalties still provide indirect stability incentives
recommended diagnostic: evaluate Method C separately

hypothesis: Method C training is not complete
evidence: seed 11 / 50 mm status=RUNNING, checkpoints=13, development_gate=False
counter-evidence: Method C has started but is not complete
recommended diagnostic: monitor the externally owned run; evaluate only after a completed development gate

hypothesis: Orchestration waits for Method B promote before Method C
evidence: run_until_success defaults ContinueAfterFailedDevelopmentGate=true and schedules C after B coverage
counter-evidence: Sequential scheduling still waits for B process completion
recommended diagnostic: fix supervisor exit-code bug

hypothesis: Method B failure incorrectly blocks Method C
evidence: failed gates are explicitly continued; supervisor attempt 3 proceeded to Method C
counter-evidence: earlier supervisor attempts failed on an empty exit-code message
recommended diagnostic: repair supervisor exit-code handling without interrupting the live run

hypothesis: Training success proxy differs from formal success
evidence: best_agent uses tracked total return, not development success
counter-evidence: environment success reward uses the same success buffer as evaluation
recommended diagnostic: evaluate checkpoint candidates on development success

hypothesis: best_agent selection is not based on development success
evidence: skrl base.py selects highest Reward / Total reward (mean)
counter-evidence: A correlation with success is possible but unverified
recommended diagnostic: rename/document as training-return-best

hypothesis: final_agent is worse than an intermediate checkpoint
evidence: no best/mid checkpoint development evaluations
counter-evidence: final gates are complete
recommended diagnostic: run fixed 5-10 scenario diagnostic when no supervisor owns Isaac

hypothesis: Curriculum restores only policy, not optimizer/normalizers
evidence: checkpoint keys include policy,value,optimizer,observation/state/value preprocessors
counter-evidence: scheduler is not checkpointed
recommended diagnostic: document whole-agent load semantics

hypothesis: Optimizer reset causes forgetting at new heights
evidence: optimizer state is in checkpoint and agent.load loads all modules
counter-evidence: KLAdaptiveLR scheduler object resets
recommended diagnostic: log scheduler state at stage boundary

hypothesis: 100 mm full randomization is introduced too early
evidence: 100 mm uses full randomization despite failed 75 mm gate
counter-evidence: fixed schedule intentionally continues failed gates
recommended diagnostic: stratify training/eval outcomes by randomization

hypothesis: 100 mm collision comes from insufficient baseline lift clearance
evidence: FSM and B share 7 rear/body-link collisions; residual is zero
counter-evidence: terminal-only collision evidence cannot reconstruct clearance
recommended diagnostic: replay collision episodes with link clearance logging

hypothesis: 100 mm collision comes from negative residual z
evidence: executed residual is zero in final collision episodes
counter-evidence: Raw actor channels can be nonzero before gating
recommended diagnostic: plot executed z by collision episode

hypothesis: 100 mm collision comes from wheel residual advancing before placement
evidence: executed wheel residual is zero and FSM has the same failures
counter-evidence: FSM reference itself commands post-transfer drive
recommended diagnostic: separate reference and residual wheel commands

hypothesis: TIMEOUTs cluster in a specific FSM phase
evidence: fsm_failure_reasons.csv and episode timelines show DRIVE_CLEAR/late-phase stalls
counter-evidence: Some global timeouts may have different transient histories
recommended diagnostic: add phase-at-timeout scalar to episodes.jsonl

hypothesis: Timeout exposes slow behavior rather than a bad timeout setting
evidence: 75 mm successes and failures run close to 150 s; phase gates stall on support
counter-evidence: The 150 s cap can still change pass/fail near the boundary
recommended diagnostic: measure required stable-dwell acquisition time

hypothesis: PPO stalls in late phases without effective progress reward
evidence: late-phase timeouts and near-zero executed residual
counter-evidence: phase-progress and recovery rewards exist
recommended diagnostic: log phase occupancy and per-phase reward

hypothesis: Success dwell and FSM completion conditions are inconsistent
evidence: phase-10 gate uses top+tilt+angular speed; success additionally requires 4-wheel upward-force support and 1.5 s dwell
counter-evidence: The stricter success predicate is intentional
recommended diagnostic: expose completion predicates side by side

hypothesis: Contact classification confuses step top and riser
evidence: classification has geometric disambiguation and tests
counter-evidence: No per-contact ground-truth opposing shape exists
recommended diagnostic: targeted contact replay with visual markers

hypothesis: CoM margin is invalid or has the wrong sign
evidence: formula is min distance to support interval; values are plausible and validity is tracked
counter-evidence: many samples are invalid and encoded zero for critic
recommended diagnostic: log invalid-rate and reason

hypothesis: Actor lacks key phase-completion information
evidence: actor lacks contact classes, forces and support margin; critic has them
counter-evidence: actor receives FSM phase/progress and proprioception
recommended diagnostic: ablate deployable contact proxies

hypothesis: Actor observation mismatches future robot feedback
evidence: perfect obstacle/detection validity/age are injected in simulation
counter-evidence: IMU, joint and velocity terms are deployment-oriented
recommended diagnostic: write real-sensor availability table

hypothesis: Domain randomization ranges are unreasonable
evidence: bounded ranges are documented; no coverage-response analysis
counter-evidence: development set uses similar bounded factors
recommended diagnostic: stratify success by friction/delay/noise/distance

hypothesis: Most training episodes never reach late phases
evidence: training phase occupancy is not logged
counter-evidence: development telemetry reaches late phases
recommended diagnostic: log phase occupancy histogram

hypothesis: Reward scales are imbalanced
evidence: large raw-action regularizers (-120/-180 per second) apply even when action is physically gated
counter-evidence: terminal success/failure weights are ±200
recommended diagnostic: log per-term returns and applied-vs-raw regularization

hypothesis: Value function learning failed
evidence: value loss exists but explained variance is not logged
counter-evidence: training stayed finite
recommended diagnostic: log explained variance and value targets

hypothesis: Entropy/exploration is inappropriate
evidence: entropy_loss_scale=0; log_std constrained to [-5,-4], giving very small exploration
counter-evidence: small exploration was intentionally chosen for FSM safety
recommended diagnostic: measure executed-action exploration after gating

hypothesis: Residual PPO only works by chance on one seed
evidence: all three seeds give the same final development success counts; none beats gate
counter-evidence: policy weights differ
recommended diagnostic: paired outcome difference table

hypothesis: Evaluation loads the wrong checkpoint or config
evidence: gate decisions hash-match final_agent and result provenance matches current configs
counter-evidence: best_agent is not evaluated by the gate
recommended diagnostic: keep explicit checkpoint/hash output in viewer
